products.description: Review "Crossroads of Life is a unique take on what makes a relationship persevere, and the author's emphasis on introversion adds to the story's originality. Bhattacharjee offers a creative and meditative plot focused on making sense of internal struggles and navigating the decision-making that impacts life events. The prose is beautifully metaphoric at times, evoking arresting images juxtaposed with lyrical writing. dialogue.user: I'm interested in the mystery books you mentioned. Can you tell me more about "Blood Orange Death (An Amanda Warren Mystery)" and "Rabbit-Trapped (Native Legends)"? Also, are there any other mystery books in my price range of $60 to $150?
dialogue.agent:
Here are the details for the mystery books you asked about:

1. **"Blood Orange Death (An Amanda Warren Mystery)"** - $12.99, Rating: 5.0, Reviews: 1, Rating Number: 3
   - Features: Amanda Warren's Next Murder...Amanda and Jace are spending a blissful week in North Carolina when her daughter Katie calls-- she's being held for questioning in the murder of popular TV finance guru Kevin Patterson. They rush back to New Jersey, where Amanda meets Jace's beautiful ex-NYPD partner, Lori Malone, the detective who's holding Katie for questioning. This case is out of Jace's jurisdiction but he and Amanda must find the killer to clear Katie's name. The stakes rise quickly as they unearth Patterson's connection to a powerful international drug cartel. Can Amanda and Jace find the killer-- and clear Katie's name-- before someone kills them first?

2. **"Rabbit-Trapped (Native Legends)"** - $7.55, Rating: 4.9, Reviews: 3, Rating Number: 13
   - Features: Ash is a teenager who wants nothing more than to escape his life and begin again somewhere far away from his family. He has the skills, determination, and even a plan to leave it all behind. But when he gets to the county line, he finds a barrier tying him to town, leaving him trapped. Neveah, wanting nothing more than a normal life, is herself trapped. Trapped in a huge house with over-protective parents, kept from school and people her own age, she longs for personal connections. When she stumbles upon a picture while scrolling the internet, her life takes a drastic turn. Elliott knows he’s different. He doesn’t fit in with other people his age - especially his stepbrother Ash - and he doesn’t want to. He prefers to spend most of his time alone…well, mostly alone. When Elliott discovers Ash and Neveah are spending time together, he comes up with a plan to separate them forever.The three teens, each trapped in their own right: one by a physical barrier he doesn’t understand, one by her family, one by a dark secret, come together in this stunning debut. Inspired by the legends of the Creek Nation, Rabbit Trapped will have you asking the question, what would you do if you could never leave?

Additionally, I found one mystery book in your price range of $60 to $150:

1. **"The Makedown"** - $62.91, Rating: 3.3, Reviews: 2
   - Description: From Publishers Weekly Anna Norton, the nasty star of screenwriter Daneshvari's unfortunate novel, was at the bottom of the social totem pole growing up. Fat, slovenly, covered in acne, she was constantly abused by her peers. As an adult, she escapes to New York and gets the Cinderella treatment from her emotionally abusive, control freak boss. With her brand-new beauty, she snags herself a hot boyfriend, but is paralyzed with fear that he will see her inner fatty and leave her. So she embarks on a secret campaign to transform Ben into a slovenly wreck. But it remains a mystery why Ben, or anyone else, would stick around. As Anna's shallow torment of the man she purports to love drags on, the watching-a-car-wreck pleasures rapidly diminish. It's like a really bad Mean Girls, executed without the insight or humor. (Feb.) Copyright © Reed Business Information, a division of Reed Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved. About the Author Gitty Daneshvari is a former Director of Development with Contrafilms in Hollywood. She is the author of SCHOOL OF FEAR, an upcoming YA project for Little Brown for Young Readers, soon to be a major motion picture for Warner Bros. She lives in LA.

dialogue.user: I'm interested in "Blood Orange Death (An Amanda Warren Mystery)" and "Rabbit-Trapped (Native Legends)". The prices are a bit low for my budget, but I'm curious about the content. Can you tell me more about the plot and characters of these books? Also, are there any other mystery books in my price range that you might recommend?
dialogue.agent:
Here are the top customer reviews for the books you're interested in:

1. **"Blood Orange Death (An Amanda Warren Mystery)"**
   - Review: "What could be worse than having your own daughter held under suspicion of murder? Not trusting the cop you love to keep an objective viewpoint when an old flame turns up, that's what! Amanda Warren grows on you. She's very human, and somehow vulnerable as she forges a new life for herself after a bitter divorce. Everything would be great, in fact, except for the unsolved murders that keep cropping up around her. Grab yourself a Blood Orange dessert, and get in on the fun and romance as Amanda works her magic on another Jersey Shore mystery. You'll love it!"

2. **"Rabbit-Trapped (Native Legends)"**
   - Review 1: "This is an amazing read! If you are looking for an exciting & interesting read, then this is the book for you! This book has an amazing story line and it will definitely keep you turning the pages to figure out what happens next. I read this book in 2 days because I could not put the thing down! Take a moment and read the first 9 pages available, you will not regret it! Happy reading!"
   - Review 2: "I really like the style of how the book is written from the point of view of each main character. It's great character development and you really get to know and understand them. Holmes writes very well. Her words captivates you and you're just enthralled. The author, the way she writes, she makes you connected to the story and her characters. You're sad when the main story is hurt. You're happy when something exciting happens and you're so angry and sometimes your skin crawls. She makes you feel all ranges of emotions and keeps you turning the pages to find out more. This to me is the mark of a great author. It's a great story line and very well written. I reccomend this book to all readers and I look forward to other books written by Holmes."
   - Review 3: "This is the perfect book for anyone who likes to figure out puzzles as you will be trying to put all the pieces together as you go along. I found it to be a charming mix of mystery and mythology and there's a random talking cat which always makes everything better. Also the characters are all very believably flawed and I found a hidden theme - the power of individual choice over the expected. All and all it was a quirky and refreshing read."
